newsitem.title: BURMA: Martial law, curfew imposed in Burma's second city.
newsitem.headline: Martial law, curfew imposed in Burma's second city.

text.p: Martial law and a curfew were imposed in Burma's second city Mandalay following recent demonstrations by Buddhist monks, diplomats and residents said on Wednesday.

Mandalay newspapers announced martial law was effective March 18 and a curfew had been imposed from 8 p.m. to 4 a.m., residents in the city said. Government officials were not available for comment but earlier this week they confirmed there had been a demonstration by monks in Mandalay.
Residents said the curfew was imposed in five townships in Mandalay, effective from Monday. Local residents said martial law had been reported in newspapers.

Diplomats said the restrictions came after weekend riots between Buddhist monks and Moslems. At least two mosques were destroyed and several people were injured in attacks that appeared to be retaliation for the rape of a young Buddhist girl by a Moslem businessman, one diplomat said.

"My understanding is that there were riots on the 15th and 16th. It seemed to be more of a socio-religious problem than a political protest," said one diplomat. Sources in the military government had said the monk demonstration occurred on Saturday.

Mandalay is the cultural centre of Burma and is home to a large number of monks. Buddhist monks played a key role in political uprisings in Burma from 1988-1990 and many were arrested after refusing to perform religious services for soldiers and their families.
